feature: Pick several layers on the picture
summary: Shift-clicking a layer on the picture adds it to what is already picked and shift-clicking a picked one drops it, and a shift-click that misses and lands on bare canvas now changes nothing instead of throwing the whole selection away.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: Open a blank canvas and draw three rectangles with the Rectangle tool, apart from each other.
Press V for the Select tool, then click the top rectangle.
Shift-click the middle rectangle. Both should be lit in the Layers list and outlined on the picture, and the Arrange row should appear in the inspector.
Shift-click empty white canvas well away from any rectangle. Nothing should change.
Shift-click the middle rectangle again. It should drop out, leaving the top one picked.
Click empty canvas with no modifier. Everything should let go.
Pick two rectangles again and press an Arrange button to line them up.

evaluate: When you shift-click and miss the layer you were aiming at, does keeping the selection feel right, or did you expect the miss to deselect?
Shift-DRAGGING on bare canvas still sweeps a fresh selection and replaces what was picked. Does that feel inconsistent next to the shift-click that spares it?
Does the Arrange row arriving on the second layer land where your eye already is, or does the inspector jumping feel unsettling?
Is it obvious enough on the picture which layers are picked, or do you find yourself checking the Layers list?
rough: A shift-click that lands on a layer swallows the press: you cannot shift-click and drag in one motion to add a layer and move the group. Moving a multi-selection on the canvas is a separate queued task and is not built yet.

Shift held during a canvas rubber band still constrains it to a square, left over from the region tools. That collides with the queued task that wants shift-drag to ADD what it sweeps, and one of the two will have to give.
Screen Recording was granted, so both pictures here are real window captures, not offscreen renders.
